fields.meta_title: Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Make a job application form that takes resumes and keeps every applicant in a table you own. Print a blank PDF for walk-ins. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline
fields.hero_description: Describe the role and what each applicant must provide. Emergent builds the job application form and the applicant table behind it, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Every Job Application Form Needs
fields.features_subheading: A job application form asks each candidate the same questions. Emergent adds role branching, uploads, PDFs and an applicant table.
fields.feature_1:
Every section, field by field

Emergent drafts the six standard sections with the right input for each answer: a date picker for the start date, a phone field and a block that repeats for each past employer.
fields.feature_2:
One form for every open role

Applicants pick a position and see only the questions written for it. A forklift operator is asked for a certification date; a bookkeeper names the accounting software they use.
fields.feature_3:
Resume and certificate uploads

Applicants attach a resume and any license or certificate the role needs from a phone, without creating an account. Each file is stored with the application it arrived on.
fields.feature_4:
Blank and filled PDF copies

Print the blank form for walk-ins at the front counter. Each application that arrives online can also be kept as a filled PDF in the same layout, ready for the personnel file.
fields.feature_5:
An applicant table with hiring stages

Every application lands as a row with role, location, stage and owner, in a table that never caps applications. The app then alerts the hiring manager by Slack or email.
fields.feature_6:
Your careers page, your source code

Publish the form on your own domain or embed it in the careers page you already run. Your developers get the full source in GitHub for anything the prompt did not cover.

fields.usecase_heading: Job Application Forms for Every Hire
fields.tab_content_1:
Know who can work weekends before you call

The first question is which store. Applicants then give a start date and tap the shifts they can work. That store's manager hears about it in Slack, and the applicant table filters by weekend availability.
fields.tab_content_2:
Catch any license due to lapse within 60 days

Each nurse gives a license number and the state that issued it, and medical assistants give their certification. Every expiry date has its own field, and the recruiter sees the flag before an interview is booked. BLS and ACLS cards upload on the same screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
Current managers hear about internal moves in private

Employees apply with their employee ID and their months in the current role. This posting asks for at least 12, and anyone short of it is told before they submit. Eligible applications reach the person's current manager as a Slack direct message and go to a table kept apart from outside candidates.
fields.tab_content_4:
The shortlist skips anyone who fails a must-have

Designers upload a resume and a portfolio, then say whether they are authorized to work in the US and what salary they expect. Anyone without work authorization, or asking above the posted band, goes to a hold list. The rest land in the design team's hiring channel in Slack as a shortlist.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Job Application Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the usual sections, then add what each role needs. Seven steps take you from a list of requirements to a published form that fills an applicant table.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what the role requires
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what you need to know before a first call: availability, location, licenses, the right to work and the pay they expect. Drop any question that would not change the decision, and never ask about age, religion or family plans. Several states also ban asking for pay history.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the sections you want, or ask for the standard set. Work history repeats for every past job the applicant lists, and references repeat the same way. The form closes with a certification the applicant signs and dates: I certify that my answers are true and complete.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name each position in the prompt along with the questions only it needs. A delivery role might ask about a driver's license and recent moving violations, while a cashier role skips both. Keep each role's extra questions to a handful, because the shared sections already carry most of the form.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which files each role requires. A resume can be optional for cashiers and required for office roles, while a cover letter stays optional everywhere. Limit uploads to PDF and DOCX files under 10 MB each.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who hears about each application and how: the store manager in Slack, the recruiter by email. Then name the stages every applicant moves through before an offer. With a stage column added, the applicant table becomes the hiring pipeline your managers filter each morning.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how paper applications get in. A QR code at the counter opens the same form on a phone, and a few blank printed copies cover anyone without one. When a paper copy comes back, a manager enters it through the online form and it joins the table.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on your careers page or your own domain, then submit a test application for every role. Check that each role shows its own questions and that the alert reaches the right person before the link goes out.

og.headline: Build a job application form you own
og.alt: Build a job application form you own, with Emergent

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Job Application Form That Feeds Your Hiring Pipeline', meta title 'Job Application Form Template and Builder | Emergent' and hero 'Emergent builds the job application form and its applicant table' cover the whole job (form, uploads, table, routing), not one feature and not new-employee or candidate-screening territory.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is mostly blank PDFs and .doc files (rocklinusd, circuit7, Iowa, Intuit, Kit Carson, swssd, DS-1950). The page yields the template content and the printable form: FAQ 3 lists the six sections field by field ('Work history, per job: employer, title, dates, reason for leaving, "May we contact this employer?"'), howto_step_2 gives the certification text, FAQ 4 answers the blank PDF first ('a free, printable job application form PDF, blank and sized for letter paper'), FAQ 7 the one-page version, feature_4 and howto_step_6 the walk-in path. Cycle-1 intent fix holds. Builder-fit, no AMBER angle; F5 pending with Divit.

specificity.evidence: Hiring variant in the table ('Prompt for the application form and the hiring pipeline around it'); buyer vocabulary throughout: 'tap the shifts they can work', 'a license number and the state that issued it', 'months in the current role', 'a driver's license and recent violations', 'Haddad_RN.pdf', 'A QR code at the counter'. No hub boilerplate.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence that says what happens: feature_1 'Emergent drafts the six standard sections...', tab_content_1 'The first question is which store.', tab_content_3 'Employees apply with their employee ID...', howto_step_6 'Decide how paper applications get in.'; FAQ answers open answer-first ('Most forms use six sections.', 'Usually not.').

craft.evidence: Two classes. (1) Tacked-on sentence: faq item 6 ends 'Others call it an employment application form.' It is appended after 'Some employers print that title at the top of the page, but the questions underneath and the signed certification do not change.', so 'Others' points back across a sentence about something else; it exists to place a secondary. Fix: fold the name into the opening ('Yes. Application for employment form and employment application form are longer names for the same document.') and end on the certification point. Only instance. (2) Serial comma used inconsistently (HUB_RULES 2a 'Consistent'). With the comma: feature_1 'a date picker for the start date, a phone field, and a block that repeats'; feature_5 'role, location, stage, and owner'; howto_step_1 'the right to work, and pay expectations'; faq item 3 'education, references, and a signed, dated certification'. Without: why_description 'The form, the applicant table and the manager alerts'; tab_image_1 alt 'a store, a start date and the shifts the applicant can work'. Pick one style and apply it to all six.

voice.evidence: (1) All four tab H3s use one formula, '[article] [modifier] application that [verb phrase]': tab_content_1 'An hourly job application that leads with availability'; tab_content_2 'A clinical job application that checks every credential'; tab_content_3 'An internal application that loops in the manager'; tab_content_4 'A professional application that sorts by must-haves'. Four in a row is the machine rhythm HUB_RULES 2b names, and HUB_RULES 5 says the tab H3 names the outcome, not the form type. Pages rewritten today do this (sales-automation 'Catch quiet deals before the forecast call'; AP 'Route each entity's bills to its own controller'). Fix: four outcome headings with different shapes, e.g. 'See who can cover weekends before you call', 'Catch a lapsing license before the interview'. (2) Three FAQ answers in a row open the same way: faq item 4 'Yes. Your form can produce...', item 5 'Yes. Ask Emergent for...', item 6 'Yes. An application for employment form is...'. Vary at least one (item 6 can open 'They are the same document.'). (3) Vague phrasing where a specific word belongs: hero_description 'every answer stays in data you own' (an answer stays in a database, not in 'data'); features_subheading 'These six pieces turn the answers into a shortlist' ('pieces' is filler, and feature_4 (PDF copies) and feature_6 (source code) have nothing to do with a shortlist). Fix: name what the six features cover, e.g. 'Below: the sections, the role branching, the uploads, the PDFs, the applicant table and where the form lives.'

truth.evidence: (1) The must-have rule in tab_content_4 is unclear and does not match the image: the copy says applicants 'answer the must-have questions: work authorization and salary range. Missing either one sends the application to a hold list.' A required question cannot be 'missing', and the copy never says what makes a salary range pass. The image's rule is a value test: 'Authorized, salary in range' / 'Salary in range, not authorized'. The mockup officeAndRemote has the same gap ('two must-have questions: work authorization and salary range. Put anyone who misses a must-have on a hold list'). Fix: state the rule in copy and mockup, e.g. 'Anyone without work authorization, or asking above the posted band, goes to a hold list.' (2) Heading overclaims: tab_content_2 H3 'checks every credential'. The body only collects a license number, issuing state and expiry and flags expiry within 60 days. Nothing is verified, and the CMA row has no check at all. Fix: say what happens ('flags a license before it lapses'). Earlier fixes verified: why_description no longer generalizes about competitors; CMA is now 'medical assistants give their certification'; tenure is checked before submit in copy and image; feature_5 says 'never caps applications'; FAQ 4 answers the blank PDF first; FAQ 9 is about roles. Table row labels 'Response limits'/'Where responses live' are pending with Divit (not failed).

distinct.evidence: The tab H3 shape is the same as the sibling creator-application's, nouns swapped. Creator-application: 'An ambassador application that recruits your best customers', 'A UGC creator application that screens for content quality', 'A creator application for an affiliate or commission program', 'A content creator application for in-house or freelance roles'. This page: 'An hourly job application that leads with availability', 'A clinical job application that checks every credential', 'An internal application that loops in the manager', 'A professional application that sorts by must-haves'. Challenger-1 flagged this class (shared 'Emergent builds the form ...' shape with creator-application) in the hero, subheading and why. Those were fixed, but the tab H3s, the same class, were not. Bodies are distinct: shift grid, license expiry, tenure gate and must-have hold list are hiring-specific. Payroll goes to new-employee-form and scored screening to candidate-screening-form (FAQ 8, FAQ 10). D2 clean. Note: tab 4's knock-out hold list sits close to candidate-screening-form's ground. Keep it to two yes/no must-haves, with no scoring.

faq.evidence: There are 10 on-topic items, each answered in its first sentence. The hub link is in item 2, with exact-match sibling links 'new employee form' (item 8) and 'candidate screening form' (item 10). One secondary does not read naturally: faq item 6 places 'employment application form' as an appended last sentence, 'Others call it an employment application form.' (see craft). The run of 'Yes.' openers in items 4, 5 and 6 is logged under voice. Other secondaries read naturally ('If HR has a fillable job application form template it likes', 'a free, printable job application form PDF').

images.evidence: (1) tab_image_3: the copy says eligible applications 'alert the person's current manager', and the timeline shows 'Current manager alerted, Priya Shah, Customer Ops'. But the Slack hero posts to the shared channel '# manager-alerts' ('Jordan Lee applied, Senior Analyst, Finance, Customer Ops, 18 months in role'). The image does not show the alert reaching Priya Shah, and it broadcasts a confidential internal application to every manager in the channel, which an HR reader will notice. Fix: make it a direct message to Priya Shah (or a card addressed 'To Priya Shah, Customer Ops'). (2) tab_image_4 draws a rule the copy never states: 'Authorized, salary in range' x3 and 'Salary in range, not authorized', against copy 'answer the must-have questions: work authorization and salary range' (see truth). Align after the copy states the band rule. Verified fixed and correct: tab 1 shift chips 'Sat AM, Sat PM, Sun PM' below 'Start date Nov 3', chip 'Shift Availability'; tab 2 'Dana Ruiz, RN, Expires in 52 days, under 60', CMA row with no state; tab 3 'Tenure checked before submit' before 'Application submitted 9:12 AM', 'Separate from outside candidates'; tab 4 shortlist 3 + hold 1 = 4. Cover and OG match tab 1. One cursor per panel, text readable, no collisions.

plan.angle: The top 10 is blank PDFs and .doc files. This page gives the finished document's content (six sections field by field, the certification wording, a one-page version and a printable blank PDF), then what a PDF cannot do: branch by role, take uploads and keep every applicant in a table that alerts the right person.
